title: Penguin Analysis in R
text:
Species Median Mass

median_mass <- penguins |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    median_body_mass = median(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

median_mass

# A tibble: 3 × 2
  species   median_body_mass
  <fct>                <dbl>
1 Adelie                3700
2 Chinstrap             3700
3 Gentoo                5000


Found the median mass of each penguin species, displayed as a table. Shows that Gentoo penguins have the largest median body mass.

title: Penguin Analysis in R
text:
Penguin Features

penguin_features <- penguins |> 
  group_by(species, sex) |> 
  summarise(
    mean_bill_length = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 
    mean_bill_depth = mean(bill_depth_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_flipper_length = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 
    mean_body_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

`summarise()` has regrouped the output.

Calculted the average features of the penguins by species and gender. Output the data as a table.

title: Penguin Analysis in R
text:
Penguin Mass Graph

ggplot(penguin_features, 
       aes(x = species, y = mean_body_mass, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Body Mass of Penguins",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Mean Body Mass (g)",
    fill = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()







Figure 1: Mean body mass of penguins by species and sex.





The graph displays the mean body mass of penguins by species and sex. Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass, while the average male penguins are larger than the average female penguins within each species.

title: My first weeks in MDS

UBC campus.


The first couple of weeks in the UBC Master of Data Science program has been a busy but exciting introduction to what the next year will look like. The first week has already involved getting familiar with new tools and workflows, working through course material, and adjusting to the pace of the program.
One of the biggest takeaways from my first week has been how much there is still to learn. Some of the technical setup has been a learning experience in itself, but I’m starting to feel more comfortable navigating these new environments. I’m looking forward to continuing to develop these skills, meeting more of my classmates, and seeing how much I can learn and accomplish throughout the MDS program.

title: Penguin Analysis in Python
text:
Penguin Mass Graph

fig, ax = plt.subplots()

penguin_features.pivot(
    index="species",
    columns="sex",
    values="mean_body_mass"
).plot(
    kind="bar",
    ax=ax
)

ax.set_title("Mean Body Mass of Penguins")
ax.set_xlabel("Species")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean Body Mass (g)")
ax.legend(title="Sex")

plt.show()







Figure 1: Mean body mass of penguins by species and sex.





The graph displays the mean body mass of penguins by species and sex. Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass, while the average male penguins are larger than the average female penguins within each species.
